title: prompt-triage: the right model, before the work starts

lines.vo: Nothing checks whether your model fits the task. This is prompt-triage, a Claude Code mod that picks the right model before the work starts.

scene.headline: The right model, {before the work starts.}

lines.vo: You pick the model before you know the task. I once left a session on Fable at high effort and forgot to switch back. That cost twenty-five percent of my weekly tokens, in one day.

scene.title: You pick the model {before you know the task.}

items.title: A new session starts on yesterday's model
25% of my weekly tokens, in one day
items.desc: Left on Fable at high effort

items.title: Nothing checks if the model fits
items.desc: Overpay for easy work, underpower hard work

lines.vo: One call to haiku at low effort rates your first prompt. Simple goes to haiku, moderate to sonnet, complex to opus, and long-running to fable. If the suggestion matches your model, there is no dialog at all.

It is a dialog, not an override. Switch moves the whole session. Keep model, effort low is offered first for simple prompts. A read-as line restates your prompt so a misread shows early. And a long-running rating offers one click down to opus.

items.title: Switch
items.desc: Move the whole session to the suggested model

items.title: Read as: line
items.desc: A one-line restatement of your prompt

items.title: Step down
items.desc: One click to opus after long-running

lines.vo: Sometimes the fix is effort, not the model. Simple keeps your model with effort low. Moderate sets a medium floor. Complex and long-running set a high floor. Run slash effort and the floor goes away.

scene.title: Sometimes the fix is {effort, not the model.}

lines.vo: Catch the leftover placeholder before you hit Enter. Say you type, make the login better, with a bracket placeholder still in it. Refine sends it to haiku for review, asks up to three questions, and rewrites the prompt into your prompt box. Nothing is sent until you press Enter.

card.title: Make the login better. [Specify the files]

lines.vo: You can refine any prompt, any time. Type slash refine-prompt, then your prompt. Pickers sit in a band above the prompt box. A refine button reviews a draft while you type. And restore original keeps your first version.

items.title: Refine button
items.desc: Review a draft while you type

lines.vo: New in zero point seven point six: one switch, whole session. Before, switching to haiku moved only the main chat. Compaction, recap and prompt suggestions stayed on the old model. Now a new fetch hook rewrites the model in those requests, just before they are sent.

steps.title: Before
steps.desc: Only the main chat moved; compaction, /recap and suggestions stayed on the old model

steps.title: Now
steps.desc: An http.fetch hook rewrites the model just before the request is sent

result.text: No /model run · your default is untouched

lines.vo: Watch the context before it costs you. A session estimate row shows cost, prompts, and tokens in context. At fifty thousand tokens, the manage context button appears. At one hundred twenty thousand, compact is recommended.

scene.title: Watch the context {before it costs you.}

steps.title: Session estimate
steps.desc: Cost, prompts and tokens in context

lines.vo: Receipts, not vibes. Slash triage-stats logs every rating, with the model before and after and the option you picked, but no prompt text. It shows the cost per decision, and it makes no model call.

items.title: Every rating logged
items.desc: Model before and after, option picked. No prompt text

items.title: Cost per decision
items.desc: Spend after it, average by rating, and effort

lines.vo: Did it save me anything? Too early to say. Five of fifteen sessions after install ran entirely on Sonnet, against none of twenty-nine before. But most of that drop is not the plugin. The rating call costs about three hundredths of a cent per session.

scene.title: Did it save me anything? {Too early to say.}

card.title: A hint, not a measurement
tags: Most of the drop is not the plugin

lines.vo: Here is where it falls short. The first prompt waits up to ten seconds. The rating can over-reach. The effort floor applies to prompt one only. State lives in memory, so a reload resets the override. Cost can be mispriced. And whether each switch was the right call is not measured yet.
Try it on a vague prompt. Open a new session, type something vague on purpose, and pick Refine prompt. It costs one small haiku request per session. If the rating gets it wrong, tell me.
